sources.what: LOA 32 ft 9.75 m, LWL 24 ft 7.31 m, beam 9 ft 6 in, draft 5 ft 6 in, displacement 9500 lb 4300 kg, lead ballast 4500 lb 2045 kg, ballast ratio 47%; alloy mast stepped on the keel; the scaled inboard profile on p. 2 (scale bar 0–8 ft), measured for the mast, the keel, the skeg and the rudder
sources.note: 15.94 px/ft by the scale bar (about 2 cm a pixel). Checks: hull length 31.56 ft (32.0), LWL 24.34 (24.0), draft 5.38 (5.50): ±2%, ±0.08 m at the mast and keel. Read off it: mast front 3.89 m aft of the stemhead (3.95 with the scale normalised to LOA; a third-party redraw reads 4.00); the keel's leading edge, a sharp-corner construction on a keel that blends into the hull, 3.86–3.94 m; trailing edge 6.52–6.62; chord 2.66 m at the hull, 1.72 at the bottom; span 0.90–1.11; leading edge swept 46°. Skeg root 7.89 m; skeg and rudder 0.99 m at the hull, the blade 0.50 at the bottom, 1.04 m below the waterline. The canoe body is 0.54–0.73 m deep at the keel's ends. The brochure's profile doesn't show the forestay.

knownGap.why: ours is 137.4° against the Wolfson report's 156°: GM (−0.8%) and maximum GZ (+4%) agree, the far end of the curve doesn't. The synthetic hull has a flat deck where she has a coachroof, and its sections are super-ellipses, not her wineglass with the ballast deep in it

ior.what: The Wolfson report's condition: IOR measurement trim, 10,112 lb, no crew

mastAftOfStem.how: read off the brochure's scaled profile: 3.89 m by its scale bar, 3.95 with the scale normalised to LOA, 4.00 on a third-party redraw

keelLeAftOfStem.how: a sharp-corner construction on the same profile (the keel blends into the hull): 3.86–3.94 m on two drawings

wlFwdAftOfStem.how: the same profile, scale normalised to LOA

balance.why: The mast, the forestay's tack and the keel are all read off an undimensioned brochure profile at about 2 cm a pixel (±2%, ±0.08–0.10 m each), her keel blends into the hull so its root is a construction, and sources give two J's (12.20 and 12.66 ft). Her stability check is the strong one: the Wolfson curve with its own inputs.

values.value: 12.66 ft (MacBar; the class's pole limit is 12.67 ft)

disagreements.effect: foretriangle 3.8% larger; with the mast read at 3.95 m the tack is 0.09 m aft of the stemhead (a redraw reads 0.17 ± 0.1)

disagreements.used: 9,500 lb in the doc (the published ratios are on it); the Wolfson figures at 10,112 lb

published.estimatedWhy: BWL is solved from the Wolfson report's BM; Tc, freeboard and every fore-and-aft position are read off the brochure's profile. BAS is a guess from the class's gooseneck height above a keel-stepped mast's butt (2.795 m), ±0.2 m. The skeg and rudder are modelled as one skeg rudder of their combined planform.
